newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL ELECTION BILL TO SKIP COMMITTEE-LEVEL VOTE.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL ELECTION BILL TO SKIP COMMITTEE-LEVEL VOTE.

text.p: A bill setting down the rules for Brazil's elections next year will skip committee-level proceedings and faces a full vote in the Chamber of Deputies either next week or the week after, a congressional official said Tuesday.
The lower house earlier approved a motion backed by government-allied political parties that makes the bill a priority in the Chamber of Deputies, the official said.
Political leaders had been divided over the details of the bill but those differences had been mostly resolved, he said.

One particularly contentious article, which would have prevented President Fernando Henrique Cardoso from inaugurating public works during his re-election campaign, will probably be dropped from the bill, the official said.
Congress must approve the bill by October 3, 12 months before the elections for president, state governors and a large number of seats in parliament.
